sessions.title: Dr. Amr Osama's PhD Defense Presentation on Lithium Niobate Microsystems
sessions.outline:
Lithium niobate (LiNbO₃) is a key ferroelectric material with remarkable optical and acoustic properties, making it essential for applications in telecommunications, sensing, and quantum technologies. The emergence of thin film lithium niobate (TFLN) has enhanced its integration potential, allowing the development of high-performance photonic and acoustic devices.

In microwave photonics, ultra-compact electro-optic modulators (EOMs) on Z-cut LN utilize spiral waveguides and top-bottom electrode configurations, achieving efficient modulation within a tiny footprint. In the RF acoustic domain, monolithically integrated wireless sensors incorporate high-Q Lamb wave resonators with meander dipole antennas, representing the first suspended LN Lamb wave devices for wireless sensing. These advancements leverage simple lithography steps for fabrication, enabling innovative solutions in photonics and acoustics.

sessions.title: MEMS Function Orientation
sessions.outline:
This session provides a structured and accessible introduction to MEMS function, going through the MEMS chip as being a core component within Si-Ware different products. It aims to give participants an overview and a clearer understanding of Si-Ware's MEMS chip. 

Session Outline: 

Introduction to MEMS: Definition of Micro Electro Mechanical Systems and the typical flow from idea to testing. 
MEMS as a Core Component: Overview of its role in the Full Stack Ownership and its interaction within the Optical Core Module. 
The MEMS Function Team & Responsibilities: Introduction to team members, main responsibilities (production, yield, supplier management), and specific roles like chip design and foundry qualification. 
Key Tools and Equipment: Details on the software (ANSYS, MATLAB) and hardware used, including the development centers in Paris and Toulouse. 
Si-Ware MEMS Chip Deep Dive: Explanation of the chip components, the Interferometer Ray Path, Critical Optical Interfaces, and the specific process layers and flow.
